note: Headless, software rendering, real mouse clicks.

results.title: <geolocation> as a canvas child
results.detail: 5768 of its 5772 pixels are drawn and getImageData() returns them. Drawn over its own box: invalid (intersection_occluded_or_distorted). Drawn 30 px away: invalid (intersection_occluded_or_distorted). Rotated: invalid (intersection_occluded_or_distorted). Outside a canvas: valid. A real click in the canvas: events click, no prompt. A real click outside: events click, promptdismiss, the browser opened its prompt.

results.title: <camera> as a canvas child
results.detail: 5690 of its 5733 pixels are drawn and getImageData() returns them. This element has no isValid property, so only a click shows whether it works. A real click in the canvas: events click, no prompt. A real click outside: events click, promptdismiss, the browser opened its prompt.

results.title: <microphone> as a canvas child
results.detail: 6860 of its 6903 pixels are drawn and getImageData() returns them. This element has no isValid property, so only a click shows whether it works. A real click in the canvas: events click, no prompt. A real click outside: events click, promptdismiss, the browser opened its prompt.

results.title: <usermedia> as a canvas child
results.detail: 10331 of its 10374 pixels are drawn and getImageData() returns them. This element has no isValid property, so only a click shows whether it works. A real click in the canvas: events click, no prompt. A real click outside: events click, promptdismiss, the browser opened its prompt.

results.title: <install> as a canvas child
results.detail: This browser has no <install> element.

results.title: A link to a visited page, with a :visited colour
results.detail: The picture has 0 pixels in the :visited colour and 1047 in the :link colour. getComputedStyle() reports rgb(0, 0, 255), the :link colour, as it does for every link. A screenshot of the same link outside a canvas has 0 pixels in the :visited colour, so this browser profile keeps no history and the row says nothing. The canvas gets the link drawn as unvisited.

results.title: System colours (AccentColor, Highlight, …)
results.detail: AccentColor rgb(0, 117, 255); AccentColorText rgb(255, 255, 255); Highlight rgb(0, 65, 198); HighlightText rgb(255, 255, 255); SelectedItem rgb(25, 103, 210); Canvas rgb(255, 255, 255); CanvasText rgb(0, 0, 0); LinkText rgb(0, 0, 238); VisitedText rgb(85, 26, 139); ButtonFace rgb(239, 239, 239); Field rgb(255, 255, 255); Mark rgb(255, 255, 0). 12 of 12 match what getComputedStyle() already reports, so the picture adds nothing script could not read before.

results.title: A checked checkbox with the default accent colour
results.detail: The box of the control reads back as rgb(0, 117, 255); AccentColor reads back as rgb(0, 117, 255). In the test browser both are the default blue. On a device with a custom accent colour the picture would carry it.

results.title: The scrollbar of a drawn scroller
results.detail: The scrollbar takes 0 px of layout width. 0 pixels of the 16 px strip at the right edge differ from the white background. This browser uses overlay scrollbars, which are hidden until the scroller moves.

results.title: Spelling markers in a text field
results.detail: The picture of a field with spellcheck on is identical to one with spellcheck off, so this browser marked nothing. The test browser has no dictionary. Try the field under "Try it by hand".

results.title: The value of a password field
results.detail: The dots are drawn. Two different passwords of seven characters differ in 0 pixels, and a password of eight characters differs in 40. The picture gives the length, which input.value.length already gives the page.

results.title: An autofill suggestion before it is accepted
results.detail: A script cannot open the autofill list. Use the form under "Try it by hand": it reports the field values, the :autofill matches and the pixels of the picture while a suggestion is previewed.

results.title: An <iframe> from another origin
results.detail: 0 of 44800 pixels of its box are drawn (44800 for the same content from this origin). getImageData() and toDataURL() do not throw, so the canvas is not tainted. The browser leaves it out of the picture, and that is why the canvas stays readable.

results.title: An from another origin, no CORS
results.detail: 0 of 24000 pixels of its box are drawn (24000 for the same content from this origin). getImageData() and toDataURL() do not throw, so the canvas is not tainted. The browser leaves it out of the picture, and that is why the canvas stays readable.

results.title: An from another origin that allows it
results.detail: 24000 of 24000 pixels of its box are drawn. getImageData() and toDataURL() do not throw, so the canvas is not tainted.

results.title: A CSS background-image from another origin
results.detail: 0 of 24000 pixels of its box are drawn (24000 for the same content from this origin). getImageData() and toDataURL() do not throw, so the canvas is not tainted. The browser leaves it out of the picture, and that is why the canvas stays readable.

results.title: A <video> from another origin, no CORS
results.detail: 0 of 24000 pixels of its box are drawn (22600 for the same content from this origin). getImageData() and toDataURL() do not throw, so the canvas is not tainted. The browser leaves it out of the picture, and that is why the canvas stays readable.

results.title: A cross-origin <iframe> uploaded as a WebGL texture
results.detail: readPixels() of the texture returns 0 non-transparent pixels for the cross-origin frame and 44800 for the same page from this origin. GL error 0. A shader gets the same empty picture a 2D context gets.

results.title: An open popover inside a drawn element
results.detail: The popover is 100 by 60 px and open over the canvas. 0 of its pixels are in the picture. The browser draws it in the top layer, above the canvas, where it takes the hit test. A canvas cannot draw, bend or read an open popover.

results.title: A modal <dialog> inside a drawn element
results.detail: showModal() opens it over the canvas and 0 of its pixels are in the picture. Like a popover it is drawn by the browser in the top layer, and it takes the hit test there.

results.title: interactivity: inert on a drawn element
results.detail: 3797 pixels of the button are drawn and elementFromPoint() does not return it. This is the opposite case to the rows above: painted, and deliberately not usable.
